---
title: 'Biometric Preference Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-03'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '81d7509dc1b0a9be2094ef9113b73402ebf5b19f'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads or writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (synchronous-getter-plus-stream shape, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed entirely by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called with an empty body to read, a `biometricEnabled` body to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the current value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read and `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (confirmed in `openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source read by both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: the switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), the PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad immediately — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers every PATCH error. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary — the fetch lives only in `features/account/`. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart` (new) — `updateSettings({bool? biometricEnabled})` → `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})`; mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/models/account_settings_dto.dart` (new) — minimal json_serializable DTO, only the response's `biometricEnabled` field.
- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart` (new) — broadcast `StreamController<bool>`, default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`) next to the auth/vault registrations.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart` (+ state, new) — wraps the repository; `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart` (new) — header + one switch row; replaces `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; its stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only when true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` alongside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] Account domain/data/DI files above -- new `features/account/` module -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `account_settings_cubit.dart` + `account_settings_screen.dart` -- optimistic toggle UI -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (a minimal screen Epic 8 later extends, never rebuilt from scratch).
- Given I reinstall the app or restart it after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh from the account, never read from a stale local-only cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape rather than `Resource<T>` (AD-12): this value is read persistently in two places (vault gate + settings screen), not fetched once on a single screen's entry — the shape `Resource<T>`'s own doc restricts it to. Defaulting to `true` before the boot fetch resolves matches current pre-2.4 behavior, so a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (the "accent = active" convention `pin_keypad.dart` deliberately avoids for itself) — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including the new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads or writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (synchronous-getter-plus-stream shape, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed entirely by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called with an empty body to read, a `biometricEnabled` body to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the current value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read and `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (confirmed in `openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source read by both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: the switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), the PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad immediately — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers every PATCH error. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary — the fetch lives only in `features/account/`. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.

- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart` (+ state, new) — wraps the repository; `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart` (new) — header + one switch row; replaces `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; its stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only when true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` alongside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] Account domain/data/DI files above -- new `features/account/` module -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `account_settings_cubit.dart` + `account_settings_screen.dart` -- optimistic toggle UI -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (a minimal screen Epic 8 later extends, never rebuilt from scratch).
- Given I reinstall the app or restart it after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh from the account, never read from a stale local-only cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape rather than `Resource<T>` (AD-12): this value is read persistently in two places (vault gate + settings screen), not fetched once on a single screen's entry — the shape `Resource<T>`'s own doc restricts it to. Defaulting to `true` before the boot fetch resolves matches current pre-2.4 behavior, so a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (the "accent = active" convention `pin_keypad.dart` deliberately avoids for itself) — no new tokens.

- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including the new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

title: 'Biometric Preference Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-03'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '81d7509dc1b0a9be2094ef9113b73402ebf5b19f'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads or writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (synchronous-getter-plus-stream shape, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed entirely by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called with an empty body to read, a `biometricEnabled` body to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the current value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read and `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (confirmed in `openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source read by both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: the switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), the PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad immediately — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers every PATCH error. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary — the fetch lives only in `features/account/`. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/{datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart, models/account_settings_dto.dart, repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart}` (new) — data source calls `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})` (mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`); DTO carries only the response's `biometricEnabled` field; repo impl is a broadcast `StreamController<bool>` default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`) next to the auth/vault registrations.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/{cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart, screens/account_settings_screen.dart}` (new) — cubit's `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix; screen is a header + one switch row, replacing `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; its stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only when true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` alongside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] New `features/account/` module (domain/data/DI, cubit, screen) -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (a minimal screen Epic 8 later extends, never rebuilt from scratch).
- Given I reinstall the app or restart it after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh from the account, never read from a stale local-only cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — this value is read persistently in two places, not fetched once on a single screen's entry (what `Resource<T>`'s doc restricts it to). Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (the "accent = active" convention `pin_keypad.dart` deliberately avoids) — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including the new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads/writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (sync-getter-plus-stream, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called empty to read, with `biometricEnabled` to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read, `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (`openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source for both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad directly — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers every PATCH error. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary — the fetch lives only in `features/account/`. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/{datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart, models/account_settings_dto.dart, repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart}` (new) — data source calls `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})` (mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`); DTO carries only the response's `biometricEnabled` field; repo impl is a broadcast `StreamController<bool>` default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`) next to the auth/vault registrations.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/{cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart, screens/account_settings_screen.dart}` (new) — cubit's `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix; screen is a header + one switch row, replacing `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; its stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only when true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` alongside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] New `features/account/` module (domain/data/DI, cubit, screen) -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (a minimal screen Epic 8 later extends, never rebuilt from scratch).
- Given I reinstall the app or restart it after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh from the account, never read from a stale local-only cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — this value is read persistently in two places, not fetched once on a single screen's entry (what `Resource<T>`'s doc restricts it to). Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (the "accent = active" convention `pin_keypad.dart` deliberately avoids) — no new tokens.

title: 'Biometric Preference Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-03'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '81d7509dc1b0a9be2094ef9113b73402ebf5b19f'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads/writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (sync-getter-plus-stream, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called empty to read, with `biometricEnabled` to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read, `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (`openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source for both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad directly — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers PATCH errors. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/{datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart, models/account_settings_dto.dart, repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart}` (new) — data source calls `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})` (mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`); DTO carries only the response's `biometricEnabled` field; repo impl is a broadcast `StreamController<bool>` default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`), next to auth/vault.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/{cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart, screens/account_settings_screen.dart}` (new) — cubit's `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix; screen is a header + one switch row, replacing `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: ...currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only if true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` beside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] New `features/account/` module (domain/data/DI, cubit, screen) -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (minimal — Epic 8 extends it, never rebuilds it).
- Given I reinstall or restart after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh, never read from a stale local cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — read persistently in two places, not fetched once on screen entry. Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads/writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (sync-getter-plus-stream, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called empty to read, with `biometricEnabled` to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read, `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (`openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source for both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad directly — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers PATCH errors. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/{datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart, models/account_settings_dto.dart, repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart}` (new) — data source calls `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})` (mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`); DTO carries only the response's `biometricEnabled` field; repo impl is a broadcast `StreamController<bool>` default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`), next to auth/vault.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/{cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart, screens/account_settings_screen.dart}` (new) — cubit's `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix; screen is a header + one switch row, replacing `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only if true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` beside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] New `features/account/` module (domain/data/DI, cubit, screen) -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (minimal — Epic 8 extends it, never rebuilds it).
- Given I reinstall or restart after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh, never read from a stale local cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — read persistently in two places, not fetched once on screen entry. Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (minimal — Epic 8 extends it, never rebuilds it).
- Given I reinstall or restart after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh, never read from a stale local cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — read persistently in two places, not fetched once on screen entry. Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.
3. **Idempotency check.** If `development_status[{story_key}]` is already at `target_status` or a later state (`review` is later than `in-progress`; `done` is later than both), return to caller — no write needed. Never regress a story's status.
4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.
5. **Epic lift (only when `target_status` = `in-progress`).** Derive the parent epic key as `epic-{N}` from the leading numeric segment of `{story_key}` (e.g., `3-2-digest-delivery` → `epic-3`). If that entry exists and is `backlog`, set it to `in-progress`. Leave it alone otherwise. Skip this sub-step entirely when `target_status` is not `in-progress`.
6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

1	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
2	
3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	
5	/// Story 2.4's one DI-singleton access point for the account's
6	/// `biometricEnabled` preference — mirrors `features/vault/domain/
7	/// repositories/vault_repository.dart`'s stream-plus-sync-getter shape
8	/// (AD-14), except the underlying source of truth is server-side (`PATCH
9	/// /account/settings`), not on-device.
10	///
11	/// [currentBiometricEnabled] is the single source both
12	/// `core/navigation/app_router.dart` (feeding `VaultLockScreen`'s
13	/// `attemptBiometricFirst`) and the Configurações toggle read — never a
14	/// second, independently-tracked copy of the same boolean.
15	abstract class AccountSettingsRepository {
16	  /// Broadcast stream of the current `biometricEnabled` preference. Like
17	  /// `VaultRepository.statusStream`, this always has a value from the
18	  /// moment the repository is constructed (`true`) — a late subscriber
19	  /// still immediately replays that cached value.
20	  Stream<bool> get biometricEnabledStream;
21	
22	  /// The last value emitted on [biometricEnabledStream], read
23	  /// synchronously — starts `true` (never `null`) so a cold boot before
24	  /// [fetchBiometricEnabled] resolves still degrades to "try biometric
25	  /// first" (Design Notes), never silent PIN-only.
26	  bool get currentBiometricEnabled;
27	
28	  /// Boot-time read: `PATCH /account/settings` called with `{}` — no GET
29	  /// endpoint exists for this resource (Boundaries). A successful response
30	  /// updates [currentBiometricEnabled]/[biometricEnabledStream] to the
31	  /// server's value; any [Failure] is swallowed (fire-and-forget, like
32	  /// `SessionRepository.restoreSession()`) and leaves
33	  /// [currentBiometricEnabled] exactly as it was.
34	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> fetchBiometricEnabled();
35	
36	  /// Story 2.4's optimistic toggle: [currentBiometricEnabled]/
37	  /// [biometricEnabledStream] flip to [enabled] immediately, before the
38	  /// `PATCH {"biometricEnabled": enabled}` call even starts (RNF01,
39	  /// <100ms) — then, on failure, revert back to the prior value and
40	  /// return `Left` so the caller can surface the `Failure`'s message. A
41	  /// successful PATCH leaves the optimistic value in place and returns
42	  /// `Right(unit)`.
43	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> setBiometricEnabled(bool enabled);
44	
45	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
46	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, same rationale as
47	  /// `VaultRepository.dispose()`/`SessionRepository.dispose()`.
48	  Future<void> dispose();
49	}

title: 'Biometric Preference Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-03'
status: 'in-progress'

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads/writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (sync-getter-plus-stream, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called empty to read, with `biometricEnabled` to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read, `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (`openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source for both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad directly — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers PATCH errors. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/{datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart, models/account_settings_dto.dart, repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart}` (new) — data source calls `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})` (mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`); DTO carries only the response's `biometricEnabled` field; repo impl is a broadcast `StreamController<bool>` default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`), next to auth/vault.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/{cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart, screens/account_settings_screen.dart}` (new) — cubit's `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix; screen is a header + one switch row, replacing `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only if true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` beside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] New `features/account/` module (domain/data/DI, cubit, screen) -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [ ] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [ ] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (minimal — Epic 8 extends it, never rebuilds it).
- Given I reinstall or restart after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh, never read from a stale local cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — read persistently in two places, not fetched once on screen entry. Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The vault's biometric gate (spec-2-1) always attempts Face ID/Touch ID first with no way to turn it off, and nothing reads/writes `biometricEnabled` server-side — Epic 1's Configurações placeholder has no real content.

**Approach:** Introduce `features/account/` with an `AccountSettingsRepository` (sync-getter-plus-stream, like `VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository`, AD-14) backed by `PATCH /account/settings` — the only account-settings endpoint, called empty to read, with `biometricEnabled` to write. Fetch once at boot, feed the value into `VaultLockScreen` so it skips biometric when disabled, and build the real Configurações screen (replacing the placeholder) around the toggle.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `PATCH /account/settings` (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/account-settings-update`) is called with `{}` to read, `{"biometricEnabled": <bool>}` to write — no GET endpoint exists (`openapi.yaml`). `AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` starts `true` (never null), the single source for both the vault gate and the toggle. Toggling is optimistic: switch flips immediately (RNF01, <100ms), PATCH fires, a failure reverts the switch and shows the `Failure`'s message. `VaultLockScreen.initState` calls `authenticate()` only when the preference is `true`; `false` shows the PIN keypad directly — PIN remains the access method regardless. Domain imports neither `flutter` nor `data/` (RNF06); repository returns `Either<Failure, T>` (RNF09).

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** No new `Failure` subtype — `Failure.fromCode` already covers PATCH errors. No change to `VaultRepository`'s contract, `vault_injection.dart`, or vault's "zero network calls" boundary. No GET endpoint invented. No `displayName`/`persona` touched (Epic 8's scope).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Boot fetch resolves `false` | `PATCH {}` returns `biometricEnabled: false` before `/vault` builds | `VaultLockScreen` skips biometric, shows PIN keypad | N/A |
| Boot fetch resolves `true` / still in flight | Returns `true`, or unresolved | `VaultLockScreen` attempts biometric first (default `true`) | N/A |
| Boot fetch fails | `PATCH {}` returns a `Failure` | `currentBiometricEnabled` unchanged | Swallowed, fire-and-forget like `restoreSession()` |
| Toggle succeeds | User taps the switch | Switch flips, persists, no error | N/A |
| Toggle fails | Network/backend error | Switch reverts to previous value | `Failure.message` shown inline |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart` (new) — `biometricEnabledStream`, `currentBiometricEnabled` (bool, starts `true`), `fetchBiometricEnabled()`, `setBiometricEnabled(bool)`, `dispose()`; mirrors `vault_repository.dart`.
- `lib/features/account/data/{datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart, models/account_settings_dto.dart, repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart}` (new) — data source calls `ApiClient.patch('account-settings-update', data: {...})` (mirrors `auth_remote_data_source.dart`); DTO carries only the response's `biometricEnabled` field; repo impl is a broadcast `StreamController<bool>` default `true`.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart` (new) — `registerAccountFeature()`, called from `injection_container.dart`'s `setupCoreDependencies()` (`:80-81`), next to auth/vault.
- `lib/features/account/presentation/{cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart, screens/account_settings_screen.dart}` (new) — cubit's `toggleBiometric(bool)` is the optimistic flip/revert from the I/O matrix; screen is a header + one switch row, replacing `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen`.
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` (new) — `BackArrowHeader` extracted from `placeholder_screens.dart`'s private `_BackArrowHeader` (`:247-280`); `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` repointed to it.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` — delete `ConfiguracoesPlaceholderScreen` (`:165-188`).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — `buildAppRouter` gains `required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository`; stream joins `_GoRouterRefreshStream` (`:52-55`); `/vault` (`:59-63`) passes `attemptBiometricFirst: accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled`; `/configuracoes` (`:91-94`) builds the new screen.
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — add `required bool attemptBiometricFirst`; `initState` (`:72-75`) calls `_attemptAuthenticate()` only if true, else sets `_showPinKeypad = true` directly.
- `lib/main.dart` — resolve `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`, fire `unawaited(fetchBiometricEnabled())` beside the existing `restoreSession()` call (`:82-84`).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] New `features/account/` module (domain/data/DI, cubit, screen) -- per Code Map.
- [x] `back_arrow_header.dart` extraction -- reuse, no duplication -- per Code Map.
- [x] `placeholder_screens.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart` -- wire the new repository + screen, remove the placeholder -- per Code Map.
- [x] `vault_lock_screen.dart` -- gate `_attemptAuthenticate()` on `attemptBiometricFirst` -- per I/O matrix.
- [x] Tests for every file above -- cover all five I/O-matrix rows -- regression coverage.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the Configurações screen opens, then it shows only the biometric toggle (minimal — Epic 8 extends it, never rebuilds it).
- Given I reinstall or restart after changing this setting elsewhere, when the app loads, then the preference is fetched fresh, never read from a stale local cache.

## Design Notes

Mirrors AD-14's stream-plus-sync-getter shape, not `Resource<T>` (AD-12) — read persistently in two places, not fetched once on screen entry. Defaulting `true` before boot-fetch resolves matches pre-2.4 behavior: a slow/offline fetch degrades to "try biometric first", never silent PIN-only. Switch active color reuses `DesignTokens.colorAccent` — no new tokens.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new account-feature and vault_lock_screen tests.

# Verification Gap Review

**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.

The main verification gap shapes are:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.

## Evidence Rules

- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Review Sequence

### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change

Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.

Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.

Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.

If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).

### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed

Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.

Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.

### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used

Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.

Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

Every test (or app run) that instantiates this singleton and then tears down via `sl.reset()` leaks that subscription, unlike the repository right above it that was given exactly this care.
  
  - **No in-flight guard on the biometric toggle allows a lost-update race.** `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl.setBiometricEnabled()` captures `previous = _currentValue` and optimistically flips before awaiting the PATCH; nothing in `AccountSettingsCubit.toggleBiometric()` or `AccountSettingsScreen`'s `Switch.onChanged` prevents two overlapping calls. If the user double-taps before the first PATCH resolves, the second call's "previous" is already the first call's optimistic value, so a failure in the first call's revert can stomp the second tap's intended end state. `vault_lock_screen.dart` already has an established pattern for this exact class of bug (`_submittingPin` guard, plus the "review finding" that now clears stale state on a fresh attempt), but it wasn't carried over to the new toggle.
  
  - **No disabled/pending visual state on the `Switch` while the PATCH is in flight** (`lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart`) — compounds the previous point: there's no indication to the user that a toggle is still being persisted, so nothing discourages the rapid double-tap in the first place.
  
  - **Cold-boot race between the fire-and-forget preference fetch and `VaultLockScreen.initState()`.** `attemptBiometricFirst` is only consulted once, in `initState()` (`lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart`). If the vault is already `locked` at boot, `/vault` builds with the default `true` and immediately calls `authenticate()`; if `main.dart`'s `fetchBiometricEnabled()` then resolves to `false` afterward, the resulting stream emission re-triggers `AppRouter`'s `refreshListenable`, but since the location hasn't changed, Flutter reuses the existing `_VaultLockScreenState` instead of re-running `initState()` — the OS biometric prompt that already fired is never retroactively skipped. Neither of the two new "Story 2.4" groups in `test/main_test.dart` nor `test/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen_test.dart` exercises this ordering (both only test the preference being already-resolved before `VaultLockScreen` builds, never "resolves after mount").
  
  - **No local persistence of the last-known preference.** `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl._currentValue` starts at the hardcoded `true` and a failed boot fetch (`main.dart`'s `_asUnchangedPreference`) leaves it there rather than falling back to a cached last-known value (e.g. secure storage). A user who previously disabled biometric and then boots while offline, or whose fetch times out, is shown the OS biometric prompt again — directly contradicting their saved choice, not merely "unchanged from an unknown state."
  
  - **Stale toggle-failure error message persists across navigation.** `AccountSettingsState.errorMessage` is cleared only at the start of the *next* `toggleBiometric()` call (`account_settings_cubit.dart`). Because `AccountSettingsCubit` is a `registerLazySingleton` — one instance for the app's whole lifetime — a failed toggle's error text is still showing if the user leaves "Configurações" and comes back later, with no new attempt made. This is the same "stale message lingers unchanged" class of bug this very diff explicitly fixed for `VaultLockScreen`'s PIN error (the "Review finding" comment in `vault_lock_screen.dart`), but the fix wasn't applied to the new screen.
  
  - **Four divergent, hand-duplicated `_FakeAccountSettingsRepository` fakes.** `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`, `test/main_test.dart`, `test/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit_test.dart`, and `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart` each define their own copy, with small behavioral drift (different default `setBiometricEnabledResult`, and one uses a `Stream.multi` replay wrapper for `biometricEnabledStream` while another uses a plain broadcast stream with an explicit comment saying replay isn't needed). The project already has a `test/support/` directory for exactly this kind of shared helper (used by `write_failure_matrix_helper.dart`), but no shared fake was factored out here.
  
  - **`dispose()` test coverage is one-sided.** `test/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`'s `dispose()` group only proves `fetchBiometricEnabled()` is a silent no-op after disposal; it never calls `setBiometricEnabled()` after `dispose()`, even though that path exercises the same `_emit()` closed-controller guard from the optimistic-flip side.
  
  - **Overly broad `catch (error)` in `AccountRemoteDataSource._patch`** (`lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart`) has no `on` clause, so it will catch and remap *any* thrown object — not just a response-shape mismatch — into `Failure.malformedResponse`. A genuine programming bug elsewhere in the decode path would be silently reported as a backend contract violation instead of surfacing as a crash during development/testing.
  
  - **No DI-wiring test for the new feature module.** There's no `account_injection_test.dart` proving `registerAccountFeature()` resolves `AccountRemoteDataSource` → `AccountSettingsRepository` → `AccountSettingsCubit` end-to-end through the real `sl` container; `main_test.dart` and `app_router_test.dart` only ever exercise it after swapping the real `AccountSettingsRepository` for a fake, so the real composition path (`AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl(remoteDataSource: sl())`, `AccountSettingsCubit(sl())`) is never actually verified to resolve without a runtime DI error.
  
  - **Unverified `Switch` API usage.** `account_settings_screen.dart` sets `activeThumbColor: DesignTokens.colorAccent` on a `Switch` — this is an unusual name versus the commonly documented `Switch.activeColor`/`thumbColor` surface. Worth confirming this parameter actually exists on the pinned Flutter 3.47.5 SDK; if it doesn't, the file fails to compile and `flutter analyze`/`flutter test` can't reach the required "zero issues."
  
  - **`AccountSettingsDto.toJson()` is dead code.** (`lib/features/account/data/models/account_settings_dto.dart`) The DTO is only ever decoded from a PATCH response (`fromJson`); nothing in the new code ever serializes one back out, so the generated `toJson()`/`_$AccountSettingsDtoToJson` is unused.
  
  - **No re-fetch of the preference after boot.** `fetchBiometricEnabled()` is only ever called once, in `main.dart`'s `initState()`. If the preference changes outside this app session (or the fetch is simply retried nowhere on failure), `currentBiometricEnabled` can stay stale — including stuck at the swallowed-failure default — for the rest of the app's lifetime, with no foreground-resume or periodic refresh to reconcile it.
</agent-message>

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.
